newsitem.title: GERMANY: Horlick takes trip to Frankfurt to plead case.
newsitem.headline: Horlick takes trip to Frankfurt to plead case.

text.p: Defiant fund manager Nicola Horlick took an impromptu trip to Frankfurt on Friday to confront the management of Deutsche Bank, saying she wanted her job back.

"There has been a very large misunderstanding...They decided to suspend me on the basis of hearsay," said the former head of pension fund business at London-based Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM).
She was suspended this week pending an internal investigation into what Deutsche Morgan Grenfell described as "a potential breach of her contract." She resigned on Thursday.
The dispute is believed to centre on allegations that she tried to take some of her MGAM team with her in a move to Dutch Bank ABN AMRO.
Horlick, 35, visibly angry, described herself as "one individual against a huge organisation" and said: "That is appalling. I am sorry, I am not going to be treated like this."

But she later struck a conciliatory tone on her way back to the airport, telling Reuters she had been given "a fair hearing" with members of Deutsche's legal and personnel departments at the bank's twin-towered headquarters in Frankfurt.

Although she failed to meet management board members, Horlick said she was "really impressed" by the attitude of the officials she met. No formal agreement was reached but she said Deutsche would now examine the allegations against her.

But relations with MGAM took a turn for the worse just before she was left when MGAM said Deutsche had met her only out of courtesy and all matters related to her former employment had to be addressed to her former employers -- MGAM.

Asked at Frankfurt airport how she reacted to MGAM's latest statement, she said: "If Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is now saying these talks were irrelevant then naturally I am very upset and want clarification."
Horlick, a mother of five, had spent the morning in a fruitless quest to speak to senior MGAM officials at the company's London headquarters.
But said said she felt vindicated by her visit to the MGAM trading floor during which, she said, she loudly proclaimed "Justice will be done," prompting some smiles from her erstwhile colleagues.
She said she was planning to take legal action against her former employer over what she called her "constructive dismissal."
Horlick also said she had been approached by many other institutions offering her new positions since her departure from MGAM.
Asked about allegations that she had planned to defect to ABN Amro, she said: "ABN Amro have refuted that and I concur with that. I was never planning a team move."
She said she never thought she would be unemployed, adding: "With a child in chemotherapy for leukaemia I am not really in a position to start a new business."
